reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch ground the no-repentance texts in God's unchanging counsel while treating the repenting texts as anthropopathic language for his grief over destroyed creatures.

discrepancy.note: Paine mocks Jonah's God as repenting of threatened judgment in plain anthropomorphic terms, incompatible with a God who cannot lie or change his mind.

quotes.text: the Ninevites reformed, and that God, according to the Bible phrase, repented him of the evil he had said he would do unto them, and did it not.
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Jonah 3:10.

sides.snippet: Yahweh was sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.
sides.verseText: Yahweh was sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.

sides.snippet: God is not a man, that he should lie, Neither the son of man, that he should repent
sides.verseText: God is not a man, that he should lie, Neither the son of man, that he should repent: Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not make it good?
